takeaways.label: 25% YoY revenue growth, broad-based
takeaways.text: Every product category and geography contributed, with oncology nearly doubling and immunosuppressants delivering high double-digit growth.

takeaways.label: Gross margin contracted ~400 bps YoY
takeaways.text: on raw material costs and power/fuel, but EBITDA margin held nearly flat at 33.0% in H1, demonstrating operating leverage.

takeaways.label: Stellon and injectables are the margin bridge
takeaways.text: Excluding these still-ramping investments, H1 EBITDA margin would have been ~37.8%, close to historical levels; meaningful Stellon revenue is expected in H2.

takeaways.label: API grew 30%, formulations only 6%
takeaways.text: as emerging-market customers shifted procurement from finished doses to API, and US business transitioned from Advergent to Stellon.

watch.label: What to watch next quarter
watch.text: Whether injectable contracts materialize in H2 as guided, the pace of Stellon’s US revenue ramp, and any easing in solvent raw material prices.

points.label: Immunosuppressants remain the core engine
points.text: High double-digit growth in H1, in line with historical rates, driven by wallet-share gains with existing customers and new market access after ANVISA inspections in Latin America.

points.label: Oncology nearly doubled YoY
points.text: Romidepsin picked up well on customer launches in the US, and Everolimus continues to see traction.

points.label: Anti-infective, antifungal, and oncology grew faster
points.text: in percentage terms, reflecting increased market penetration for products commercialized in the last couple of years.

points.label: Nystatin poised for a step-change
points.text: Several US customers have qualified Concord as a source and validation quantities have been supplied; once commercial supplies begin, management expects a significant jump.

points.label: Fusidic acid and Fidaxomicin are new contributors
points.text: Fusidic acid expected to commercialize in emerging markets in the next few months to a quarter, then extend globally; Fidaxomicin launched and a US DMF has been filed, seeing good traction.

points.label: Customer additions concentrated in newer segments
points.text: Several new customers added in the last six months, particularly in anti-infectives, antifungal, and oncology.

points.label: Pricing strategy is discount-led but margin-preserving
points.text: Concord gained customers by offering significant price discounts versus incumbent suppliers while maintaining API-business profitability, thanks to economies of scale, fermentation expertise, and productivity; no pricing pressure was experienced.

quotes.text: Ankur Vaid: "We have been able to gain customers by reducing their procurement cost, but at the same time it has been in line. So, we haven't seen any pricing pressure when it comes to Concord, but yes, we have been able to gain customers because of the price reduction compared to their current existing suppliers."

points.label: API revenue grew 30% YoY; formulation revenue grew only 6%
points.text: due to a shift in procurement strategies across emerging markets, where certain customers opted to procure API instead of finished formulations, and the transition of US business from Advergent to the wholly owned subsidiary Stellon Biotech.

points.label: Domestic formulation grew 29% in Q2
points.text: , above the company average, and is expected to continue growing above the company average as own manufacturing for injectables comes online and drives capacity utilization.

points.label: Domestic revenue grew 42% YoY; export revenue grew 8%
points.text: , but including deemed exports, the overall export contribution would be significantly higher because customers are shifting procurement to Indian subsidiaries from where products are subsequently exported to regulated markets.

points.label: Management urges evaluating overall business growth
points.text: rather than viewing API and formulation revenues in isolation, since the focus is on expanding end-customer sales and wallet share irrespective of the routing.

quotes.text: Ankur Vaid: "At Concord, we believe it is more appropriate to evaluate the overall business growth rather than view API and formulation revenues in isolation. Our focus remains on expanding end-customer sales and increasing our wallet share, irrespective of whether the business is routed through API or formulations."

points.label: Gross margin contracted ~400 bps YoY
points.text: , primarily driven by an increase in raw material prices, particularly solvents, amidst ongoing geopolitical uncertainties and broader supply chain disruptions, plus higher power and fuel costs partly offset by renewable energy investments made last year.

points.label: EBITDA margin held nearly flat
points.text: H1 FY27 at 33.0% versus 33.2% in H1 FY26, demonstrating operating leverage and business model resilience despite the gross margin hit.

points.label: The Stellon/injectable drag is material and temporary
points.text: Excluding expenses associated with the new injectable facility and Stellon, where revenues are yet to ramp up, H1 FY27 EBITDA margin would have been ~37.8%, closer to historical levels. Q2 FY27 EBITDA margin excluding these expenses would have been 37.1%.

points.label: Formulation gross margins are optically depressed
points.text: because API is transferred to formulation units at market price, not COGS; at low utilization (Unit-IV at 5%), this shows an adverse picture on gross margins, so management advises looking at EBITDA margins instead.

points.label: Raw material cost pass-through is not the preferred path
points.text: Management finds it challenging to pass on raw material cost increases to customers and prefers addressing them through R&D and productivity improvements, viewing these as short-term issues.

points.label: Power and fuel benefits are still to come
points.text: As power and fuel costs stabilize, the company expects to realize the full benefits of renewable energy investments, providing further support to the overall margin profile.

quotes.text: Ankur Vaid: "It is quite challenging, I would say, to pass on some of the costs that we have incurred to the customers. I think, we would rather try to address these issues through R&D and through productivity improvements rather than passing these, because these are again more of a short-term issues."

sections.title: Stellon, Injectables & the US Formulation Build-Out

points.label: Stellon traction is starting now
points.text: Materials and finished products have been supplied to Stellon for the US market; meaningful revenue contributions are expected in H2 FY27, and the ramp-up will help move reported EBITDA from 33-34% toward 38-39%.

points.label: Tofacitinib already supplied to Stellon
points.text: Mycophenolate Mofetil oral suspension expected to be supplied in the next quarter.

points.label: Injectable contracts are in advanced discussion
points.text: The company is actively engaging with several large domestic and global customers and expects to finalize contracts in H2 FY27; securing them would drive higher utilization of the injectables manufacturing facility.

points.label: Several customer audits completed
points.text: Multiple inspections and audits by potential injectable customers were conducted in the last couple of months.

points.label: Domestic injectable ambition is sized
points.text: The injectable TAM is ~₹5,000 crore; a ₹300 crore top-line target over 3-4 years from domestic and export markets is considered achievable if target customers come on board.

points.label: US formulation presence is nascent but seen as having significant potential
points.text: to emerge as a meaningful contributor to growth over the coming years.

sections.title: New Initiatives: CDMO, Inspira Dermatology & Pipeline

points.label: CDMO is live with one commercial project
points.text: Concord is the exclusive manufacturer for a third-party innovator's NCE product launched ~1.5 years ago, currently at a ~$2 million annual run-rate; the customer believes the opportunity could be much larger. Additional smaller projects are in development stages.

points.label: Inspira dermatology division launched
points.text: Focused on eczema, anti-infectives, antifungals, and acne products (Tacrolimus, Pimecrolimus, Fusidic acid, Nystatin, Mupirocin, Mupirocin calcium); Concord is the only company in India fully integrated from API to finished product in this range. Reaching ₹400-500 crore would take at least 4-5 years.

points.label: Pipeline of 10-15 products
points.text: with significant capacities already built to cater to requirements once they become commercial; management sees a lot of potential in these products as growth drivers for the API business.

points.label: Regulatory milestones support the pipeline
points.text: ANDA approvals received for Tofacitinib and Mycophenolate Mofetil Oral Suspension; US DMF filed for Fidaxomicin; USFDA inspection of Unit-II formulation facility successfully completed; ANVISA approval received for Unit-III facility at Limbasi.

points.label: Base API growth expected slightly above the historical 18-19%
points.text: H1 grew at 26% with fair visibility on Q3; FY27 growth is expected to be "slightly better" than the historical rate because work that did not fructify last year due to customer risk aversion is materializing this year.

points.label: Beyond API, injectables, CDMO, and finished formulations
points.text: are expected to drive growth beyond the historical 18-19% trajectory.

points.label: FY28 and beyond, management expects to continue 18-20%+ growth
points.text: , framing last year's degrowth as a global phenomenon, not structural.

points.label: Competitive advantage rests on a fermentation-based API portfolio
points.text: that management claims no other Indian company matches, plus a strong pipeline of products nobody in India is developing; the company sees an opportunity to take significant market share from European and Southeast Asian competitors.

points.label: Immunosuppressant growth is structural
points.text: Driven by underlying market growth of ~10% and second-source conversions, which are the bigger contributor.

points.label: New products like Nystatin and Fusidic Acid
points.text: are expected to see a significant volume surge as FDA approvals come through in regulated markets.

quotes.text: Ankur Vaid: "I would say that there is no company like Concord which has such a vast portfolio of fermentation-based APIs, and we continue to build on that portfolio." Ankur Vaid: "We have a very strong pipeline of products which nobody in India is developing and I think our competition coming from Europe or Southeast Asia, we see a good position that we will be able to take significant market share on those products."

items.title: Injectables Unit IV ramp-up
items.text: The Valthera injectables facility, commercialized March 2025 and WHO-GMP certified in FY26, is running at ~5% utilization, with customer contracts expected to materialize in H2 FY27. Management targets ~₹300 crore of injectables revenue over 3-4 years and full breakeven in FY28, which would lift margins from 33-34% toward the historical 38-40%.

items.title: Stellon US commercial launch
items.text: Stellon Biotech, the wholly owned US subsidiary, takes over the US business from Advergent, with the transition impacting formulation revenue in H1 FY27 and meaningful revenue expected from H2 FY27. Fresh ANDA approvals - Tofacitinib (US market ~US$500 million) and Mycophenolate Mofetil Oral Suspension (~US$30 million) - give it products to push, and its ramp-up is one of the levers to restore historical margins.

items.title: Nystatin and Fusidic Acid scale-up
items.text: Nystatin, a Para IV product, has been qualified by several US customers and supplied validation quantities, with commercial supplies yet to begin and a significant jump expected once they start. Fusidic Acid, commercialized in FY26 with limited European competition, begins European supplies once CEP approval lands and should contribute meaningfully this and next financial year.

items.title: CDMO fermentation contracts
items.text: CDMO is just 1-2% of sales today, and management intends to make it a double-digit contributor, with one exclusive animal-health project already commercialized (~a couple of million dollars annually) and at least one more project expected to commercialize this year. Internally it targets 4-5 opportunities worth around $40-50 million, supported by 1,250 m³ of fermentation capacity and cost advantage versus Europe and China.

items.title: Second-source and innovator API wins
items.text: Concord is entering as second source with aggressive pricing on existing products, with conversions seeded 8-12 months ago landing in Q1 FY27 and more at advanced discussion stages. It began supplying two innovator companies in FY26, with a couple more projects expected to reach closure by end of FY27, and ₹79.3 crores of FY26 CWIP included plant modifications for one such larger-volume project.

items.title: New API launch cadence
items.text: The portfolio of 30+ products is set to add 2-3 launches annually from a 10-15 product pipeline, with recent DMF filings including Pimecrolimus, Voclosporin, Romidepsin and Fidaxomicin. Voclosporin, where only ~3 global players exist, has filed and is supplying validation batches, with commercial sales across global markets expected next year.

items.title: Inspira dermatology division
items.text: Inspira, launched mid-2026, targets a ~₹5,000 crore Indian dermatology market where Concord is the only fully API-to-finished-product integrated player, with management guiding ₹400-500 crore over four to five years. A smaller facility for the topical range is being set up and should be visible in FY27.

items.title: Renewable power margin gains
items.text: Captive renewable investments - a 27.38% stake in FSGE Renewable Power Private Limited for the Limbasi plant and a June 2026 agreement for a wind-solar hybrid project - have started delivering savings worth ~1-1.5% of EBITDA. With power and fuel ~20% of cost, further fuel-cost improvement pushes the benefit toward the 1.5% mark.
